In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aprA and npra genes are not required for production of the Cry1Bb insecticidal protein, that deletion of these genes does not affect the insecticidal activity of the protein, and that deletion of these two genes increases the amount of Cry1B protein produced.

the deletion of the nprA gene from a Bt strain does not have a negative effect on the production of insecticidal crystal protein and that the deletion of nprA and aprA genes from a Bt strains does not have a significant effect on the insecticidal activity of the insecticidal crystal.
the deletion of nprA and aprA genes from the genome of Bacillus thuringienses subsp. kurstkii strain HD-1 (Btk) resulted in the enhancement of the production of the crystal protein Cry1Bb.

The main takeaway from our work is that

protease-deficient mutants of B. thurigensis can be used to increase yields of crystal proteins and that these protease-deficient strains can be used to produce insect-resistant transgenic crops without the need for protease inhibitors in the plant.
the aprA1 and nprA1 genes can be deleted from a strain of B. thuringiensis without affecting the yield of the Cry protein and without significantly changing the toxicity of the Cry protein.
